  - Watchdog story a5014bb4: latency up on POST /api/v1/datatable/{screenid}/{activerecordid} in runtime-core-api, 07:19-08:07Z (monitor 236570583 Triggered 07:20:03Z, Recovered 08:38:03Z)

  - 100% of >3s spans on that resource are from agxcel2.method.me (12 root spans, max 12.96s). 0 errors: 0 trace errors, 0 runtime-core-api error logs, 0 agxcel2 error logs

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #54 (lifetime).
Monitor: [CRM][P2] notifications P95 latency high (#alert-runtime-monitoring, fired 09:31:07Z)
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience`
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: re-query p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod} over the monitor's own last_10m window plus a wider surrounding window -- expect values in the 0.001-0.2s range, nowhere near 1s. 2) Check 0 error logs on service:notifications for the window (not yet separately conf…
Open Jira: none

*Root-cause analysis*
  • Triggered 09:31:07Z, Recovered 09:41:07Z. This is the same 09:31:07Z fire time as 11-23 and 11-25. `p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod} by {resource_name}` 09:25-09:40Z: get_/signalr/reconnect 86,209.8s @09:30Z (a ~23.9h connection-lifetime span), get_/signalr/connect 14.99s, post_/signalr/poll 14.96s. Every request/response resource was <0.2s. This confirms the 11-21 addendum mechanism: long-lived SignalR transport spans inflate p95. The ~24h span length explains why the fire lands at 09:31Z every day.
  • DD logs `service:notifications status:error` 09:20-09:45Z: 0
  • Reasoning: matches the KB shape and the evidence reproduced this cycle, so this is a known-issue recurrence.
